Int. Your editor — late night

Your agent wrote three versions. You can only see one.

Agents are great at trying things. But every idea lands in a different branch, and comparing them means stashing, checking out, reinstalling and rebuilding, then comparing memory to reality. Screenshots don’t click.

$ git stash
$ git checkout pricing-minimal
$ pnpm install
$ pnpm dev
# wait… what did the bold one look like?
$ git checkout pricing-bold
$ pnpm dev
Without Screenplay · one branch at a time
With Screenplay · every branch built, running and clickable
Ext. The canvas — day

From one prompt to a wall of working prototypes.

Screenplay turns “what if we tried…” into something everyone can click.

Scene 1

Point it at a repo

Add a repository and Screenplay boots its dev server in a sandbox, live on the canvas.

Scene 2

Call for takes

Ask for three directions. Each gets a Workspace: a real git branch with its own running sandbox.

Scene 3

Watch them all run

Frames appear side by side as they build. Click through them, resize to mobile, point at anything.

Scene 4

Print the winner

Keep iterating on the one you love, then open a pull request straight from the canvas.

Int. The writers’ room — continuous

Everything a canvas needs to direct a room full of agents.

Real sandboxes, not screenshots

Every frame is a live dev server on its own branch. Click, scroll, fill in forms, flip to mobile.

Multiplayer by default

Share a link. Everyone sees the same canvas, cursors, comments and running branches.

Point at anything

Press ⌘E, click an element in any frame, and send it to the agent.

Knobs for every take

Expose spacing, color and copy with @screenplay.space/knobs and tune every branch at once.

Bring your own harness

Claude Code, Codex or opencode, with the models you already pay for.

Local-first on your Mac

Git worktrees for sandboxes and your installed CLIs for agents. Your code stays put.

The Screenplay cast

Open source, down to the props.

Screenplay is MIT licensed. Run the desktop app, self-host the multiplayer web app, or swap in your own sandbox, blob store and models.

Questions from the audience
What is Screenplay, exactly?

A canvas for coding agents. Every Workspace is a git branch with its own sandbox and dev server, rendered as a live frame, so you compare results side by side instead of one checkout at a time.

Which agents does it work with?

Claude Code, Codex and opencode, using your existing CLIs and accounts.

Does my code leave my machine?

Not with the desktop app. Sandboxes are git worktrees on your disk and agents are the CLIs you’ve installed.

What does it cost?

Nothing. Screenplay is MIT licensed. You bring your own agent subscriptions or API keys.
